title: Model evaluation — sales lens cheat sheet
summary: One-page operational brief for AE and solutions teams that translates model-catalog signals (open models + verified profiles) into tight sales talking points, deal-level heuristics, and a simple competitive contrast matrix. Focus: speed to close, reduce technical back-and-forth, and reduce buyer uncertainty about model quality and fit.
audience: Account Executives, Solutions Engineers, GTM leadership, Pre-sales
key_messages: Verified profiles are a signal, not a guarantee: they reduce discovery time by surfacing testable model behaviors and known failure modes.
Open models unlock choice and cost leverage for customers — position as flexibility + auditability vs closed-provider lock-in.
Redwood’s catalog ties model behavior to operational levers (quantization, batching, routing) so buyers can trade cost <-> latency <-> quality predictably.
We provide short, shareable artifacts that shorten PoC cycles: benchmark snippets, prompt tests, and rollback/variant playbooks.
When customers ask about ‘best model’, reframe to ‘best-for-your-workload’ using workload signals (latency SLO, token mix, safety requirements).
positioning_comparisons: Redwood: catalog emphasizes measured model behavior + deployment knobs (dedicated/private) — sells to engineering-led buyers concerned about cost and latency.
Closed-provider APIs: simple choice, strong marketing but limited control — sell to product teams that want fast setup and fewer ops responsibilities.
Self-hosted OSS runtimes: high control and lower long-term cost but heavy ops — sell to platform teams with infra bandwidth and strict compliance needs.
Other managed inference vendors: vary on guarantees and tooling; highlight Redwood’s unified runtime + rollout/observability story as a tie-breaker for reliability-conscious buyers.
objections_and_rebuttals: Objection: 'Open models are lower quality than closed models.' Rebuttal: Verified profiles show measured failure modes and curated prompt templates; quality varies by workload — we recommend lightweight evals with customer prompts in the first week.
Objection: 'We don't want more vendor complexity.' Rebuttal: Position Redwood as simplifying serving operations: single API + consistent rollout policies across hosted/dedicated/private modes.
Objection: 'How do I know the model will stay stable?' Rebuttal: Explain model pinning, versioned profiles, and rollback mechanics in Console; share sample SLOs and regen/playback tests.
Objection: 'Open models sound risky for compliance.' Rebuttal: Offer Private deployment and KMS/HSM integrations; verified profiles include audit notes and known-data-handling behaviors.
Objection: 'We need predictable cost.' Rebuttal: Show Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization) tied to measured unit economics from similar workloads.
Objection: 'We already use another provider.' Rebuttal: Run a quick, deterministic comparison using one shared prompt and token-limited latency targets — our benchmark snippets make this low-effort.
recommended_playbook_steps: 1) Pre-call: pick 2 candidate models from catalog (one high-quality, one cost-optimized) and prepare a 3-prompt suite that mirrors the customer's core usage.
2) Discovery call: capture workload signals (avg request length, concurrency, latency SLOs, privacy constraints). Share a short explainer on verified profiles.
3) Fast PoC: run the 3-prompt suite for both models in Redwood's sandbox, export per-token costs and latency percentiles, and deliver a 48-hour report.
4) Decision checkpoint: map results to customer's SLOs and recommended deployment (hosted for speed, dedicated for throughput, private for compliance).
5) Rollout plan: propose a canary with automatic fallback to a cheaper variant and a clear rollback window; include alerts for quality regressions tied to customer prompt tests.
6) Commercial: use measured savings from Optimize to justify reserve vs pay-as-you-go; show deterministic unit economics for 6- and 12-month horizons.
example_pitch_snippets: 'We don't say 'best' models — we say 'best for this workload.' Let us run your 3 representative prompts and show you real latency, cost, and quality numbers within 48 hours.'
'Our verified profiles mean you don't need to take model claims at face value — we measure hallucination, instruction-following, and latency across representative scenarios.'
'Want predictable pricing? We'll run the PoC with batching and quantization settings and show the expected cost per 1,000 requests — you can pick the tradeoff that fits your economics.'
'If you need private hosting or KMS-backed keys, we can show an enterprise deployment plan that preserves the same API and rollout behavior.'
open_questions: What are the minimum dataset examples we ask customers to provide to make the 48-hour PoC credible?
Do we need a templated legal addendum for early private PoCs that includes data handling promises?
Which 3 canonical prompts should we standardize on for text summarization/QA/chat/translation to improve cross-deal comparability?
How should we instrument the PoC report so engineering buyers can immediately import suggested settings into their infra-as-code?
